clinicalPearls: A disorder of failed or incomplete cleavage of the embryonic forebrain (prosencephalon) into two hemispheres, graded as alobar, semilobar, lobar, and the middle interhemispheric variant
In alobar holoprosencephaly imaging shows a single midline monoventricle with fused thalami and absent interhemispheric fissure and corpus callosum

Because forebrain and midface arise together, the severity of brain malformation often parallels the facial anomaly, from cyclopia and proboscis to hypotelorism, single central incisor, and cleft lip or palate

Causes include chromosomal abnormalities, notably trisomy 13, single-gene variants in the sonic hedgehog pathway such as SHH, ZIC2, SIX3, and TGIF1, and environmental factors including maternal diabetes
Endocrine dysfunction is common because the hypothalamic-pituitary axis is midline, so diabetes insipidus and other pituitary deficiencies should be sought
Clinical features include developmental delay, epilepsy, hypotonia or spasticity, dysautonomia with temperature instability, and feeding difficulty
Diagnosis combines prenatal ultrasound and foetal or postnatal MRI with karyotype, microarray, and single-gene testing for counselling
reference.pathophysiology: Holoprosencephaly arises from failure of ventral induction and midline patterning of the developing forebrain in early gestation, when the prosencephalon should cleave into paired cerebral hemispheres and lateral ventricles. Disruption of the sonic hedgehog and related signalling pathways, whether from single-gene variants, chromosomal imbalance, or environmental insults such as maternal diabetes, prevents normal separation of midline structures. The result is a spectrum from complete non-cleavage with a monoventricle and fused deep grey nuclei to milder incomplete separation, with parallel disruption of midline facial development.
additionalDifferentials: Severe hydrocephalus with a dilated single-appearing ventricle
Agenesis of the corpus callosum with interhemispheric cyst
additionalInvestigations: Prenatal ultrasound and foetal MRI to assess forebrain cleavage and facial structures
Postnatal brain MRI to grade the malformation and detect associated anomalies
Karyotype and chromosomal microarray to detect trisomy 13 and other imbalances
Single-gene or panel testing for SHH, ZIC2, SIX3, and TGIF1
Endocrine evaluation of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis including assessment for diabetes insipidus
redFlags: Diabetes insipidus with dangerous sodium and fluid disturbance
Temperature instability and dysautonomia in the neonatal period
Severe facial malformation with airway or feeding compromise
reference.prognosis: Prognosis correlates with the severity of the malformation. Alobar holoprosencephaly usually results in death in utero or early infancy, whereas milder lobar forms may allow survival with variable degrees of developmental disability, epilepsy, and endocrine dysfunction.
pitfalls: Assuming a normal karyotype excludes a genetic cause when single-gene pathway variants may be responsible
Missing hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, particularly diabetes insipidus, in the neonatal period
Mistaking severe hydrocephalus or hydranencephaly for alobar holoprosencephaly on imaging
Overlooking the maternal diabetes association during counselling and future pregnancy planning
management: Provide supportive and palliative care matched to severity, recognising that severe alobar forms are often lethal in early infancy
Diagnose and replace pituitary hormone deficiencies, notably desmopressin for diabetes insipidus and anterior pituitary hormone replacement
Manage feeding difficulty and failure to thrive with nasogastric or gastrostomy feeding, and address temperature instability from dysautonomia
Treat spasticity, hypotonia and developmental delay with physiotherapy, occupational and speech therapy
Correct associated midline facial anomalies such as cleft lip and palate with a craniofacial surgical team
Refer to clinical genetics for karyotype, microarray and sonic hedgehog-pathway gene testing, with counselling on recurrence and maternal glycaemic control in future pregnancies
Coordinate multidisciplinary paediatric neurology, endocrinology and developmental care
